items.title: Dave McKenna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: and then I did a record date with him for a Japanese label in June in New York, with Michael Moore and Jake Hanna, there was four of us.

ctx.x: Harry, gee he’s so young too.

He’s playing great. I went — Frank Tate, the bass player took a band to Ireland and England last November, and Harry knocked me out. I knew he played well, he’s far beyond that now, and then I did a record date with him for a Japanese label in June in New York, with Michael Moore and Jake Hanna, there was four of us. And I really enjoyed that too.
Anybody in particular writing tunes today that you think may become standards?

items.title: Michael Moore interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: And then you have somebody like Dave McKenna, which is like a whole orchestra by himself.

ctx.x: He has some groups. And Becky Kilgore and Dave have recorded together so they have material to work from. And then you have somebody like Dave McKenna, which is like a whole orchestra by himself. And so Joe knows how to do it and he knows how to mix guys — like Cal and I doing a duo together, and we have played together over the years. And he knows, to a degree, what’s going to work. And it’s just again, there’s not many groups around anymore, except a few very famous ones.
I wanted to play something for you, and see if you recognize this.
